# gcore_waap_domain_custom_rule (Resource)

WAAP custom rules allow, block, challenge, monitor or tag requests to a domain when all of their conditions match.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "gcore_waap_domain_custom_rule" "example_waap_domain_custom_rule" {
  domain_id = 1
  action = {
    allow = {
      foo = "bar"
    }
    block = {
      action_duration = "12h"
      status_code = 403
    }
    captcha = {
      foo = "bar"
    }
    handshake = {
      foo = "bar"
    }
    monitor = {
      foo = "bar"
    }
    tag = {
      tags = ["string"]
    }
  }
  conditions = [{
    asn = {
      asns = [1]
      negation = true
    }
    content_type = {
      content_type = ["application/xml"]
      negation = true
    }
    country = {
      country_code = ["Mv"]
      negation = true
    }
    file_extension = {
      file_extension = ["pdf"]
      negation = true
    }
    header = {
      header = "Origin"
      value = "value"
      match_type = "Exact"
      negation = true
    }
    header_exists = {
      header = "Origin"
      negation = true
    }
    http_method = {
      http_method = "CONNECT"
      negation = true
    }
    ip = {
      ip_address = "ip_address"
      negation = true
    }
    ip_range = {
      lower_bound = "lower_bound"
      upper_bound = "upper_bound"
      negation = true
    }
    ja3 = {
      ja3_fingerprints = ["e7d705a3286e19ea42f587b344ee6865"]
      negation = true
    }
    ja4 = {
      ja4_fingerprints = ["t13d3113h2_e8f1e7e78f70_ce5650b735ce"]
      negation = true
    }
    organization = {
      organization = "UptimeRobot s.r.o"
      negation = true
    }
    owner_types = {
      negation = true
      owner_types = ["COMMERCIAL"]
    }
    request_rate = {
      path_pattern = "/"
      requests = 20
      time = 1
      http_methods = ["CONNECT"]
      ips = ["string"]
      user_defined_tag = "SQfNklznVLBBpr"
    }
    session_request_count = {
      request_count = 1
      negation = true
    }
    tags = {
      tags = ["string"]
      negation = true
    }
    url = {
      url = "/wp-admin/"
      match_type = "Exact"
      negation = true
    }
    user_agent = {
      user_agent = "curl/"
      match_type = "Exact"
      negation = true
    }
    user_defined_tags = {
      tags = ["SQfNklznVLBBpr"]
      negation = true
    }
  }]
  enabled = true
  name = "Block foobar bot"
  description = "description"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `action` (Attributes) The action that the rule takes when triggered. Only one action can be set per rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action))
- `conditions` (Attributes List) The conditions required for the WAAP engine to trigger the rule. Rules may have between 1 and 5 conditions. All conditions must pass for the rule to trigger (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions))
- `domain_id` (Number) The domain ID
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether or not the rule is enabled
- `name` (String) The name assigned to the rule

### Optional

- `description` (String) A human-readable description.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The unique identifier for the rule

<a id="nestedatt--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action`

Optional:

- `allow` (Map of String) The WAAP allows the request
- `block` (Attributes) WAAP block action behavior could be configured with response status code and action duration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action--block))
- `captcha` (Map of String) The WAAP presents the user with a captcha
- `handshake` (Map of String) The WAAP performs automatic browser validation
- `monitor` (Map of String) The WAAP monitors the request but takes no action
- `tag` (Attributes) WAAP tag action gets a list of tags to tag the request scope with (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action--tag))

<a id="nestedatt--action--block"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action.block`

Optional:

- `action_duration` (String) How long a rule's block action will apply to subsequent requests. Can be specified in seconds or by using a numeral followed by 's', 'm', 'h', or 'd' to represent time format (seconds, minutes, hours, or days). Empty time intervals are not allowed. If not specified, the action is applied only to the request that triggers the rule.
- `status_code` (Number) An HTTP status code that the WAAP returns if a rule blocks a request.
Available values: 403, 405, 418, 429.


<a id="nestedatt--action--tag"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action.tag`

Required:

- `tags` (Set of String) The list of user defined tags to tag the request with



<a id="nestedatt--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions`

Optional:

- `asn` (Attributes) Match the ASN (Autonomous System Number) the request originated from, as determined by a WHOIS lookup of the requesting IP (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--asn))
- `content_type` (Attributes) Match the requested Content-Type (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--content_type))
- `country` (Attributes) Match the country that the request originated from (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--country))
- `file_extension` (Attributes) Match the incoming file extension (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--file_extension))
- `header` (Attributes) Match an incoming request header (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--header))
- `header_exists` (Attributes) Match when an incoming request header is present (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--header_exists))
- `http_method` (Attributes) Match the incoming HTTP method (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--http_method))
- `ip` (Attributes) Match the incoming request against a single IP address (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--ip))
- `ip_range` (Attributes) Match the incoming request against an IP range (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--ip_range))
- `ja3` (Attributes) Match the JA3 TLS client fingerprint of the request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--ja3))
- `ja4` (Attributes) Match the JA4 TLS client fingerprint of the request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--ja4))
- `organization` (Attributes) Match the organization the request originated from, as determined by a WHOIS lookup of the requesting IP (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--organization))
- `owner_types` (Attributes) Match the type of organization that owns the IP address making an incoming request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--owner_types))
- `request_rate` (Attributes) Match the rate at which requests come in that match certain conditions (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--request_rate))
- `session_request_count` (Attributes) Match the number of dynamic page requests made in a WAAP session (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--session_request_count))
- `tags` (Attributes) Matches requests based on specified tags (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--tags))
- `url` (Attributes) Match the incoming request URL (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--url))
- `user_agent` (Attributes) Match the user agent making the request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--user_agent))
- `user_defined_tags` (Attributes) Matches requests based on user-defined tags (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--user_defined_tags))

<a id="nestedatt--conditions--request_rate"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions.request_rate`

Required:

- `path_pattern` (String) A regular expression matching the URL path of the incoming request
- `requests` (Number) The number of incoming requests over the given time that can trigger a request rate condition
- `time` (Number) The number of seconds that the WAAP measures incoming requests over before triggering a request rate condition

Optional:

- `http_methods` (List of String) Possible HTTP request methods that can trigger a request rate condition
- `ips` (List of String) A list of source IPs that can trigger a request rate condition
- `user_defined_tag` (String) A user-defined tag that can be included in incoming requests and used to trigger a request rate condition

<a id="nestedatt--conditions--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions.tags`

Required:

<a id="nestedatt--conditions--url"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions.url`

Required:

- `url` (String) The pattern to match against the request URL.
Constraints depend on `match_type`:

- **Exact/Contains**: plain text matching (e.g., `/admin`, must comply with `^[\w!\$~:#\[\]@\(\)*\+,=\/\-\.\%]+$`).
- **Regex**: a valid regular expression (e.g., `^/upload(/\d+)?/\w+`). Lookahead/lookbehind constructs are forbidden.

Optional:

- `match_type` (String) The type of matching condition.
Available values: "Exact", "Contains", "Regex".
- `negation` (Boolean) Whether or not to apply a boolean NOT operation to the rule's condition


<a id="nestedatt--conditions--user_agent"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions.user_agent`

Required:

- `user_agent` (String) The user agent value to match

Optional:

- `match_type` (String) The type of matching condition.
Available values: "Exact", "Contains".
- `negation` (Boolean) Whether or not to apply a boolean NOT operation to the rule's condition


<a id="nestedatt--conditions--user_defined_tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions.user_defined_tags`

Required:

- `tags` (Set of String) A list of user-defined tags to match against the request tags

Optional:

- `negation` (Boolean) Whether or not to apply a boolean NOT operation to the rule's condition

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import gcore_waap_domain_custom_rule.example '<domain_id>/<rule_id>'
```
